sentences.text: 3. The brief facts of the case are that on 03.07.1999 at about 10:30 AM, Sri S.B. Yadav, the Food Inspector found the revisionist carrying milk for sale which was told to him to be mixed milk of buffalo and cow and on a suspicion of the same to be adulterated he stopped the revisionist and purchased 600 mili liter milk and prepared the receipt and other documents on which the revisionist is said to have refused his signature.
The sample was then treated with solution of formalin and sealed in three bottles in equal quantity.
The process of sealing and labelling was done and then one of the bottles was sent to the Food Analyst, U.P., Lucknow for analysis.
The Food Analyst vide his report dated 18th August, 1999 opined that the said sample was deficient in milk fat by less than 22% and solid non fat by less than 13%.
The proceedings then were taken up on the recommendation of the applicant before the C.M.O. and then a complaint dated 18.06.1999 was filed by the said Food Inspector.

The trial in the matter started in which after framing of charges,
three witnesses, namely, S.K. Rai, Food Inspector (P.W.-1), Subhash Chandra Srivastava, the Chief Food Inspector (P.W.-2) and Vinod Kumar Singh, Food Clerk in the office of C.M.O. (P.W.-3) were examined.
The accused in his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. denied the prosecution case.

The Food Inspector Sri Samar Bahadur Yadav, who had taken the sample and had done the proceedings thereafter had died and, as such, S.K. Rai (P.W.-1) was produced, who identified his handwriting before the trial court and gave evidence regarding the same.
The trial court finding the prosecution case to be beyond reasonable doubt and finding that the milk, which was mixed milk is adulterated convicted the revisionist as aforesaid.
The revisionist preferred an appeal before the Sessions Judge concerned, which was dismissed by the judgement and order dated 20.07.2016.
Against the said judgement and order, the present criminal revision is preferred before this Court.

4. Learned counsel for the revisionist has raised a short argument before this Court that since the Food Inspector Sri Samar Bahadur Yadav had died and was not produced before the trial court, the proceedings at the time of taking of the sample from the revisionist-accused could not come on record.

It is further submitted that even the reading of the complaint does not go to show that the milk, which was suspected to be adulterated from which sample was drawn was homogenized by the said complainant/officer at the time of drawing of its sample.
It is further submitted that the said Food Inspector, who had drawn the sample of milk could not be produced before the trial court.
The fact that the said milk from the container was initially homogenized and then sample was drawn could not come on record, if the same was done.
It is further submitted that the prosecution thus would be dented, if there was not credible evidence of the milk being homogenized and then sample of it being taken.

It is further submitted that since the same is lacking in the present matter, the present revision is a fit revision, in which benefit of doubt should be extended to the revisionist and the impugned judgement and orders be set aside.

5. Learned AGA for the State although per contra opposed the revision but did not dispute the fact that the Food Inspector Sri Samar Bahadur Yadav, who had drawn the sample had died since P.W.-1 has himself stated that the said officer has died and thus he had appeared before the trial court for identifying his handwriting.

Learned AGA for the State further could not dispute the fact that there is nothing on record to show that the milk was first homogenized and then sample was drawn from it, which was then sent to the public analyst for its testing.

sentences.text: It is not an uncommon fact that the milk unless homogenized will have different consistencies in the storage can.

Since there is nothing on record to show that the milk was homogenized prior to its sample being drawn, which was sent for testing and found deficient of milk fat and solid non fat only and was not found to be adulterated with any other extraneous material, it is a fit case, in which benefit of doubt needs to be extended to the revisionist.
7. In view of the discussions as above, this Court extends the benefit of doubt to the revisionist.
The revision is allowed.
The judgement and orders impugned are set aside.
Revisionist is on bail, he need not surrender.
The bail bonds are cancelled and sureties are discharged.
8. Office is directed to transmit the copy of this judgement to the trial court forthwith for its compliance and necessary action.
